div.head: II Atr 1.2
div.ab: ⁊ ælc ðæra landa ðe ænigne friðige ðæra ðe Ænglaland hergie, beo hit utlah wið us ⁊ wið ealne here.
Et omnis terra, quę aliquem eorum manuteneat, qui Angliam inquietant, sit exlex apud nos et omnem exercitum.
⁊ ælc ðæra landa ðe ænigne friðige ðæra ðe Ænglaland hergie, beo hit utlah wið us ⁊ wið ealne here.
Und jedes der Länder, das irgend einem derer Friedensschutz gewährt, welche England verheeren, das gelte geächtet bei uns und beim ganzen Heere [der contrahirenden Nordleute].
And every one of the lands that gives protection to any of those who harry England, let it be outlawed by us and by the whole army [of the contracting Northmen].
And every region which affords protection to any of those who harry England shall be treated as an enemy [country] by us and all the aforesaid fleet.
And any region which gives asylum to any of those who are harrying England is to be treated as an enemy by us and the whole army.

note.seg: Hierunter sind nicht nur Normandie, Wales, Irland, Schottland gedacht, sondern auch jede Englische Provinz, die eigenmächtig fremden (England feindlichen) Wikingern die Landung erlauben würde
By this are meant not only Normandy, Wales, Ireland and Scotland, but also any English province that might, on its own authority, allow foreign Vikings (hostile to England) to land
S. Gl Dänen 14a; friedlos 8. a. Vermutlich dürfen solche Länder von beiden Kontrahenten bekriegt und dorther kommende Schiffe, Fremde und Waren gefangen werden
See Gl Dänen 14a; friedlos 8. a. Presumably such countries may be made war upon by both contracting parties, and ships, foreigners and goods coming from there may be seized
It is not clear whether landa here denotes English provinces or independent neighbouring kingdoms.
Does this mean, as Liebermann suggests, that such regions might be warred upon by either party to the truce and their ships and wares seized?
